sections.h2: Who collects property tax in Milwaukee County?
sections.html:
It depends on where the house is and whether the bill is current or delinquent. The Milwaukee County Treasurer collects delinquent property taxes for 2024 and earlier years for every Milwaukee County municipality except the City of Milwaukee. The City of Milwaukee Treasurer collects both current and delinquent taxes on properties inside the city.

Assessment is local. The Wisconsin Department of Revenue tells owners to contact the local assessor about the value of a property and the local clerk about the tax bill. In Milwaukee County that means your own city or village, since the county has 19 municipalities, 10 of them cities and 9 of them villages.

Milwaukee County is the only Wisconsin county that is completely incorporated. No part of it has the unincorporated town status found elsewhere in the state, so every parcel sits inside a city or village.

sections.h2: What is Milwaukee County like for someone selling a house with taxes due?
sections.html:
Milwaukee County is the most populous and most densely populated county in Wisconsin. The 2020 census counted 939,489 residents, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 924,216, a decline of 1.6 percent. About 241 square miles are land, and another 948 square miles are water, for 1,189 square miles in all. The city of Milwaukee is the county seat. Other large municipalities include West Allis, Wauwatosa, Greenfield, Oak Creek and Franklin.

  • Housing units: 429,425 (July 2025 estimate).
  • Owner-occupied rate: 49.9 percent, so about half of households rent (2020 to 2024).
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $230,700.
  • Median gross rent: $1,101 a month.
  • Median household income: $64,435.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 1,046.

A buyer or title company will look for delinquent amounts on the parcel before closing, so know what the Treasurer's records show before you list.

sections.h2: When are Wisconsin property taxes due and what do late payments cost?
sections.html:
The state's 2026 Guide for Property Owners says an owner who pays in installments owes the first payment by January 31 and the second by July 31, unless the local government set a different schedule. If the first installment is not received within five working days after January 31, the entire unpaid balance is delinquent as of February 1. A late payment later in the year makes the balance delinquent on the first day of the following month.

The state guide adds that some counties impose an extra penalty of 1.5 percent per month, and that an owner who never pays may lose the property.

sections.h2: How do I pay a City of Milwaukee property tax bill?
sections.html:
The City Treasurer accepts payment by mail, in a drop box, by phone or online. The office is at City Hall, Room 103, 200 East Wells Street, Milwaukee, WI 53202, and the customer service line is 414-286-2240. Cash is not accepted.

  • Mail a check with the return envelope from your bill, mailing early because the Postal Service moved its postmarking to regional centers on December 24, 2025.
  • Use a drop box: inside City Hall at the Market Street entrance and outside the Municipal Building on Market Street are open around the clock, and one at the Broadway entrance is open when the building is open.
  • Pay online by ACH from a checking or savings account, or by card with a 2.75 percent convenience fee ($3.00 minimum).
  • Sign up for the ten-month interest-free installment plan if your real estate bill is over $100 and you can make the first payment by January 31.

The City Treasurer says online and phone payments are scheduled to go offline on Monday, November 30, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. for system maintenance and the annual bill update. Special charges and assessments left unpaid by mid-November may be added to the tax bill, and those cannot be appealed or negotiated.

sections.h2: How do I pay delinquent taxes to the Milwaukee County Treasurer?
sections.html:
The County Treasurer's office offers three paths for delinquent taxes: online, by mail or in person at the Milwaukee County Courthouse. Online payment runs through Value Payment Systems, which charges 2.55 percent of the total for credit or debit cards and a flat $1.50 for e-checks. The county receives no part of that fee.

The Treasurer's records list every unpaid delinquent tax, penalty and interest charge, and parcels with nothing owed show a zero balance. A payment made today may not appear until one business day later. If a listed amount looks wrong, call the Treasurer at (414) 278-4033, the same number to ask about a monthly payment plan.

The office collects back taxes through payments, Wisconsin Tax Refund Intercept (TRIP), foreclosure or a lawsuit against the individual. Parcels in bankruptcy are not subject to foreclosure or collection except as federal bankruptcy law allows. The Treasurer points out that paying quickly is cheaper because of the 18 percent yearly charge, and suggests a home equity loan or mortgage refinance as possible ways to cover the bill.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Milwaukee County property assessment?
sections.html:
Wisconsin assesses non-agricultural property at its market value as of January 1, and each municipality has to be within 10 percent of market value at least once every five years. If you disagree with your value, start with the assessor, then attend the Open Book period, when the assessment roll is open for examination. The Board of Review begins at least seven days after Open Book opens.

To object at the Board of Review, you must give the clerk written or oral notice of your intent at least 48 hours before the first meeting. Then submit the Objection Form for Real Property Assessment (PA-115A), which counts as filed if the clerk receives it within the first two hours of that meeting. A property owner can ask the board to waive the hearing and go straight to circuit court, but a granted waiver ends the right to claim an excessive assessment or appeal to the Department of Revenue. A court action under section 70.47(13) must begin within 90 days of the waiver notice.

Disputes over exemptions skip the Board of Review. An owner contesting exempt status files a claim of unlawful tax with the municipality by January 31 of the year the tax is payable, under section 74.35. Your city or village clerk can tell you the Board of Review dates.

sections.h2: What should a seller do about taxes when a Milwaukee County house is sold?
sections.html:
Look up the parcel before you list or accept an offer. For a property outside the City of Milwaukee, use the County Treasurer's online search or call (414) 278-4033. Inside the city, use the City Treasurer's resident access system or call 414-286-2240. Ask the title company to confirm payoff amounts for the current year, delinquent years and any special charges.

If taxes stay unpaid, Milwaukee County uses the in rem foreclosure process, in which title to a delinquent property can be transferred under Wisconsin law. The county does not sell foreclosed properties for back taxes. It sells them at fair market value, as with any other property. Lender foreclosure auctions run separately, with the Sheriff holding them on Monday mornings and advising buyers to check for delinquent taxes first.

After the sale, the new owner should record the change with the Milwaukee County Register of Deeds. The City Treasurer says that if the former owner's name is still on a city tax bill, the new owner should tick the change-of-address box on the payment coupon so a refund check does not go to the previous owner. Mailing address changes are also reported to the City Assessor at City Hall, Room 507.

faqs.q: Who do I pay if my Milwaukee County property taxes are delinquent?
faqs.a: Pay the Milwaukee County Treasurer unless the house is in the City of Milwaukee. Inside the city, the City of Milwaukee Treasurer collects both current and delinquent taxes. The County Treasurer's number is (414) 278-4033, and the City Treasurer's customer service line is 414-286-2240.

faqs.q: What interest does Milwaukee County charge on late property taxes?
faqs.a: The Milwaukee County Treasurer says state law requires it to charge 18 percent delinquency charges per year. The Wisconsin Department of Revenue describes interest of 1 percent per month back to February 1, plus an additional 1.5 percent per month penalty in some counties.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Milwaukee County?
faqs.a: Installment payers owe the first half by January 31 and the second half by July 31 unless the local government set a different schedule. A missed first installment makes the whole balance delinquent as of February 1 once five working days have passed.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Milwaukee County delinquent taxes with a credit card?
faqs.a: Yes, through the county's online payment system. Value Payment Systems charges a 2.55 percent convenience fee for credit or debit cards and a flat $1.50 for e-checks. Milwaukee County gets none of that fee.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my assessment in Milwaukee County?
faqs.a: You must give the Board of Review clerk notice at least 48 hours before the first Board of Review meeting and file the PA-115A form within the first two hours of that meeting. Contact your city or village clerk for the exact dates, because they differ by municipality.
